newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania tries alleged 1991 coup plotters.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania tries alleged 1991 coup plotters.

text.p: Lithuania began the trial on Tuesday of 52 people accused of organising and backing the 1991 Soviet crackdown against the Baltic state's independence bid in which 13 people were killed.

Of the 52 accused of backing the crackdown, only six defendants are actually present in the courtroom, four are already dead, and the rest are believed to be living in Belarus and Russia, a court spokesman told Reuters.
Lithuania began its fight to quit the Soviet Union in the late 1980s and infuriated Moscow by declaring independence in March 1990.
The crackdown came on the night of January 13, 1991, when Soviet troops stormed the television tower in Vilnius, which thousdands of ordinary Lithuanians were protecting behind makeshift barricades.
One woman was crushed under a tank and the rest were shot in what was one of the bloodiest indicidents in the collapse of the Soviet empire.
The two key defendants are Mikolas Burokevicius and Juozas Jarmalavicius, who face the death penalty if found guilty.
However, capital punishment was recently suspended by presidential decree and the country is moving to scrap it.
The other defendants face between three and ten year prison sentences.
Burokevicius and Jarmalavicius were leaders of the pro-Moscow remains of the Lithuanian Communist Party, most of which had in 1989 seceded from the all-mighty Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

The trial began with the reading of the indictment which runs to 13 volumes of between 250 and 300 pages each. The total trial papers run to thirteen such volumes and around 4,000 people are expected to give evidence both in court and in writing.
